title: FeverPAIN
subtitle: Acute sore-throat antibiotic decision support
summary: FeverPAIN supports antibiotic decisions in acute sore throat alongside assessment for airway compromise, deep-neck infection and sepsis.
population: People aged 3 years or over with an acute infective sore throat and an examinable pharynx; evidence is limited in very young children.
exclusions: Assess febrile children under 5 using the appropriate fever pathway.
Do not delay emergency assessment for airway compromise, severe systemic illness or suppurative complications.

criteria.label: Attend rapidly: symptoms began within the previous 3 days

results.label: Do not offer antibiotics for uncomplicated acute sore throat
actions: Advise fluids and suitable analgesia; explain that symptoms commonly last about 1 week
Advise prompt help for rapid or significant worsening or systemic illness, or if improvement has not begun after 1 week

results.label: Consider no or back-up antibiotic
interpretation: Consider no antibiotic or a back-up prescription according to the clinical picture and local antimicrobial guidance.
actions: Consider no antibiotic with safety netting, or a back-up prescription
If issued, advise use if improvement has not started within 3 to 5 days or symptoms worsen rapidly or significantly
Advise prompt medical help for marked worsening or systemic illness

results.label: Consider antibiotic
interpretation: Consider an immediate or back-up antibiotic according to the clinical picture and local antimicrobial guidance.
actions: Consider an immediate or back-up antibiotic after clinical assessment; if treatment is indicated, phenoxymethylpenicillin is first line, with alternatives guided by allergy, pregnancy and current local policy
Advise prompt medical help for marked worsening or systemic illness

overrides: Escalate immediately for suspected airway compromise. Refer to hospital for severe systemic infection or a severe suppurative complication such as quinsy, deep-neck abscess or Lemierre syndrome.

People who are systemically very unwell, have signs of a more serious condition or are at high risk of complications need an immediate antibiotic decision under the relevant pathway regardless of score.
limitations: The score does not exclude epiglottitis, peritonsillar abscess, retropharyngeal infection or sepsis.
